ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Mumtaz Mahal

code.originalText: Prenatal visit at 34 weeks: growth scan, postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment, delivery plan, and contraception counseling

text.paragraph: Prenatal visit at 34 weeks after six weeks of travel; growth scan and birth planning. [S]

Mumtaz Mahal returns at 34 weeks 2 days, three days after coming back from six weeks of travel with her family. The visits planned at 30 and 32 weeks did not take place: the family moved several times and no clinic was arranged, and no blood pressure was checked while she was away. She has felt well. She has had no headache, visual change, upper abdominal pain, swelling of the face or hands, breathlessness, bleeding, leaking fluid, or regular contractions; she has occasional painless tightenings, and the baby moves often. She took aspirin and folic acid throughout. The test-of-cure urine culture sent before she left grew nothing. She is staying in the city until the birth. She had the growth scan this morning. She has thought about the future and says she wants her body to rest after this baby. [S]

list.item:
Fourteenth pregnancy at 37 (O09.529). Blood pressure 112/70 mmHg, urine protein negative, and no symptoms of preeclampsia after the missed visits. Normal growth on the 45th centile, cephalic, normal fluid. Hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL and platelets 228. EPDS 5 with item 10 scored 0. [S]
Weekly visits from now until the birth, with blood pressure and urine protein each time.
Group B streptococcus swab at 36 to 37 weeks.
Weekly fetal heart rate monitoring from 36 weeks, which can be offered at her age.
Induction of labor at 39 weeks at the hospital, which she chose after discussing the options; continue aspirin until delivery.

Grand multiparity: postpartum hemorrhage risk (O09.40). Postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment: thirteen previous vaginal births (a major risk factor for uterine atony); anemia now corrected; no previa, accreta, multiple pregnancy, or large baby; no bleeding disorder; no previous hemorrhage that she knows of. Medium risk. [S]
Birth at the hospital, which has a blood bank, 24-hour anesthesia, and an operating theatre; she will not travel again before the birth.
On admission: blood count, type and screen, and two large-bore intravenous lines.
Labor: timely assessment of progress so that labor is not prolonged; her past labors were short, so she should come in at the first regular contractions.
Third stage: oxytocin 10 units intramuscularly or intravenously as the baby is born, controlled cord traction, uterine tone checks, and quantitative measurement of blood loss.
If hemorrhage is diagnosed (blood loss of 1000 mL or more, or any loss with signs of shock): tranexamic acid 1 g intravenously over 10 minutes within 3 hours of birth, a second 1 g dose if bleeding continues after 30 minutes or restarts within 24 hours, uterine massage, second-line uterotonics, and escalation through the hemorrhage protocol.
Anesthesia consultation at 36 weeks.

Short interpregnancy interval (O09.899). She wants her body to rest and does not want another pregnancy for at least two years; she has not decided whether she wants more children. She asked which methods are acceptable within her faith; we discussed that many Muslim scholars permit reversible contraception, and she can speak with a religious adviser of her choosing. [S]
Options reviewed: implant, hormonal or copper IUD, progestin-only pill, injection, lactational amenorrhea, and permanent methods.
She chose an etonogestrel implant placed before she leaves hospital after the birth; it is safe with breastfeeding.
Advised waiting at least 18 months, and preferably 24 months, after this birth before any future pregnancy.
